title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's sequel to La Longue Marche (pp. 650 bis–787), on topological surfaces with marked points and their Teichmüller groups. On the previous pages he takes a topological group G acting by homeomorphisms on (X,S). For each x in I (I = S, the set of punctures) he considers a punctured disc neighbourhood Δ*_x and its universal cover. He builds a group G̃ of pairs (u, ũ), where ũ is a germ of a lift of u to these universal covers near the punctures. He topologises it (topology of uniform convergence of the lifts and of their inverses) and admits that G̃ → G is a covering of topological groups with kernel ∏_x T_x. Here T_x ≅ π_1(Δ*_x) is the deck group, a free rank-one abelian group.

This page:
(135) When X is an orientable connected surface, let T be the rank-one group attached to its two orientations, so that T ≅ Z canonically once an orientation is chosen. Then every T_x is canonically isomorphic to T.
(136) The exact sequence (128) becomes 1 → T^I → G̃ → G → 1.
(137) The universal case is G = 𝒜 = Aut_top(X,S), the homeomorphism group with the topology of uniform convergence of u and u^{-1}.
(138) In the anabelian (hyperbolic) cases, where (X,S) has type (g,ν) with 2g−2+ν > 0, one knows that the identity component 𝒜^0 is contractible. So 𝒜 is an extension of a discrete group by 𝒜^0. Consequently the extension 𝒜̃ of 𝒜 descends to the discrete level.
(139) It comes from an extension 1 → T^I → 𝒯̃ → 𝒯 → 1 of the Teichmüller group.
(140) 𝒯 = 𝒯(X,S) = 𝒜/𝒜^0 = π_0(Aut_top(X,S)), the full (orientation-reversing allowed, puncture-permuting) mapping class group.

On the next page 𝒯̃ is called the 'special Teichmüller group' Sp 𝒯. For general G, an action amounts to a continuous homomorphism G → 𝒜, and by functoriality G̃ is the pullback of 𝒯̃ along G → π_0(G) → 𝒯.

In modern terms, 𝒯̃ is essentially the mapping class group of the surface with the punctures blown up into boundary circles (homeomorphisms fixing the boundary pointwise, extended by the permutations and orientation-reversals of 𝒯). Equivalently, it is the mapping class group 'with tangential base points / framings at the punctures'. Restricted to the pure, orientation-preserving part, it is the classical central extension of Γ_{g,ν} by Z^ν generated by the boundary Dehn twists. The purpose is preparatory: these twists along the punctures are needed before returning, on the next page, to a local analytic or algebraic structure near I.
errors: Minor: when G permutes the points of I or reverses orientation, T^I is not central in G̃. G acts on T^I by permuting the factors and through the orientation character. The text does not say this, but nothing is wrong.
The 'anabelian' list (g,ν) ≠ (0,0),(0,1),(0,2),(1,0) is correct for 2g−2+ν>0, i.e. 2g+ν≥3.

The contractibility of 𝒜^0 is stated as known (Hamstrom; Earle–Eells, Earle–Schatz for the smooth case) and is correctly used. The well-definedness of the topology on G̃ is explicitly admitted ('J'admets que tout marche') on the previous page, so there is a gap left unproved, though the claim is true.

ideas.what: Extension of the homeomorphism group / mapping class group by Z^I via lifts to universal covers of punctured disc neighbourhoods
ideas.modern_name: Mapping class group of the surface with boundary (or with tangential base points/framings) as a central extension of Γ_{g,ν} by Z^ν (boundary Dehn twists)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Birman, Harer et al.); tangential base points: Deligne 1989, Ihara
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme / Longue Marche discuss the Teichmüller tower and surfaces with boundary; the 'Sp T' terminology unsure

ideas.what: Contractibility of the identity component of Homeo(X,S) in hyperbolic cases, so that 𝒯 = π_0(Homeo)
Universal case: any G-action is pulled back from Aut_top(X,S), so G̃ is the pullback of the special Teichmüller extension
ideas.modern_name: Pullback of the universal central extension of the mapping class group

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but standard construction of the boundary/framed mapping class group as an extension of the Teichmüller group by Z^I, using known contractibility results. The named 'special Teichmüller group' is a minor terminological curiosity, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: Around (138): the reading is roughly 'alors on sait que 𝒜^0 est [connexe et] contractile, donc 𝒜 extension de [discrete group] par 𝒜^0 ...'. The words 'extension' and 'contractile' are insertions above struck text.
'l'extension \hat{𝒜} de G' should read 'l'extension 𝒜̃ de 𝒜' (tilde over 𝒜).
In (139) the first term T^I is written over a struck-out symbol.
